name: opportunity
paper_title: Collecting complex activity datasets in highly rich networked sensor environments
authors: Daniel Roggen, Alberto Calatroni, Mirco Rossi, Thomas Holleczek, Kilian Foerster, Gerhard Troester, Paul Lukowicz, David Bannach, Gerald Pirkl, Alois Ferscha, Jakob Doppler, Clemens Holzmann, Marc Kurz, Gerald Holl, Ricardo Chavarriaga, Hesam Sagha, Hamidreza Bayati, Marco Creatura, Jose del R. Millan
venue: 2010 Seventh International Conference on Networked Sensing Systems (INSS), pp. 233-240, IEEE
license: CC BY 4.0 (dataset, per UCI). Conference paper (c) IEEE; PDF is ETH/EPFL green OA author version.
notes: CANONICAL dataset paper for the OPPORTUNITY Activity Recognition dataset (a.k.a. OPPORTUNITY/OPP). Full study: 72 sensors of 10 modalities in 15 wireless/wired networked sensor systems, deployed in a room reproducing a studio flat; 12 subjects performing morning-routine ADLs, >25 hours of sensor data. UCI-released ML-ready subset ('OPPORTUNITY Activity Recognition Data Set', DOI 10.24432/C5M027): 4 subjects, 6 runs each (5 ADL sessions + 1 'drill'), 242 columns = 145 body-worn (7 IMUs + 12 3D accelerometers) + 60 object (12 instrumented objects) + 37 ambient (13 switches, 8 3D accel). Body-worn/object sensor streams provided at 30 Hz (the sampling rate used in the OPPORTUNITY challenge). Annotation is multi-level: Locomotion (stand/walk/sit/lie), 17 mid-level gestures + Null, and high-level ADLs; a heavy Null class makes it a standard benchmark for on-body HAR. COMPANION/CHALLENGE PAPER (cite alongside for the benchmark protocol): Chavarriaga, Sagha, Calatroni, Digumarti, Troester, Millan, Roggen, 'The Opportunity challenge: A benchmark database for on-body sensor-based activity recognition', Pattern Recognition Letters 34(15):2033-2042, 2013, DOI 10.1016/j.patrec.2012.12.014. Dataset license per UCI: CC BY 4.0. The INSS conference paper itself is (c) IEEE; PDF here is the ETH/EPFL green open-access author version from infoscience.epfl.ch.
